body.statement:
Fix \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta>0\), \(M_1>0\), and \(M_2>M_1^2\), and put \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\) and \(q_C=(C-1)/C\).  There are constants \(0<c_{\mathrm{unif}}\le C_{\mathrm{unif}}<\infty\) and \(T_{\mathrm{unif}}<\infty\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\) and not on \(C\) or on any alphabet cardinality, such that, simultaneously for every \(C\ge1\) and \(T\ge T_{\mathrm{unif}}\),
\[
 c_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}
 \le R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 \le C_{\mathrm{unif}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}.
\]
The upper bound is attained by the observable estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}\), where \(\kappa_T(C)=0\) if \(Tq_C^2\le1\), and otherwise
\[
 \kappa_T(C):=\min\!\left\{\left\lfloor T/2\right\rfloor,
 \left\lfloor\frac{\log(Tq_C^2)}{2\log(1/\alpha)+\log L}\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
The converse holds against every measurable estimator.  It is witnessed by a binary-action, bounded-reward subclass of the finite-action conditional-moment model.  Hence the exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), equivalently \(C-1\asymp T^{-1/2}\) near \(C=1\), and there is no logarithmic factor in the risk.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 r:=\log(1/\alpha)=1/t_0,
 \qquad D:=2r+\log L,
 \qquad x:=Tq_C^2.
\]
Because \(t_0,\zeta>0\), one has \(r>0\), \(L>1\), and \(D>0\).  Moreover
\[
 \beta=\frac{2r}{D}=\frac{2}{2+t_0\zeta},
 \qquad 1-\beta=\frac{\log L}{D}. \tag{10}
\]

For the upper bound, use \(\mathrm{lem{:}radius\text{-}sensitive\text{-}phiw\text{-}envelope}\).  Since \(0\le q_C<1\), \(x\le T\).  Thus there is a finite \(T_{\mathrm{unif}}\), depending only on \(D\), such that \(\log T/D<T/2\) for all \(T\ge T_{\mathrm{unif}}\); consequently the cap by \(\lfloor T/2\rfloor\) is inactive for every \(C\ge1\) at those sample sizes.

If \(x\le1\), then \(\kappa_T(C)=0\), and the envelope gives
\[
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_0-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le4M_1^2q_C^2+\frac{2A_{\mathrm{ph}}}{T}
 \le\frac{4M_1^2+2A_{\mathrm{ph}}}{T}. \tag{11}
\]
If \(x>1\), put \(k=\lfloor\log x/D\rfloor\).  The floor inequalities and (10) give
\[
 q_C^2\alpha^{2k}\le\alpha^{-2}q_C^2x^{-\beta},
 \qquad
 T^{-1}L^k\le T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}. \tag{12}
\]
The two quantities on the right have the same value:
\[
 q_C^2x^{-\beta}=T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}
 =T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}. \tag{13}
\]
Equations (12)--(13) and the envelope therefore imply, uniformly over the class,
\[
 E_M[(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}-\theta(K,e))^2]
 \le C_{\mathrm{up}}\left\{T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\right\}, \tag{14}
\]
where \(C_{\mathrm{up}}\) depends only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\).  The estimator uses only \(\mathsf O_T\), the revealed policies and alphabets, and the displayed fixed constants, so (14) is a valid witness for the infimum in \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\text{-}risk}\), not an oracle family.

We next derive a testing inequality used for both lower bounds.  Let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) be mutually absolutely continuous laws with respective target values \(+a\) and \(-a\), where \(a>0\).  Put \(R=dP_+/dP_-\),
\[
 A:=\int\sqrt{dP_+dP_-},
 \qquad O:=\int\min(dP_+,dP_-).
\]
Concavity of the logarithm gives
\[
 \log A=\log E_{P_+}[R^{-1/2}]
 \ge E_{P_+}[\log R^{-1/2}]
 =-\tfrac12\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-). \tag{15}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the product of the square roots of the smaller and larger densities gives
\[
 A^2\le O(2-O)\le2O. \tag{16}
\]
For any estimator, classify as plus when its value is positive.  On either classification error its squared loss is at least \(a^2\), and the sum of the two error probabilities is at least \(O\).  Hence (15)--(16) imply
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,+1\}}E_v[(\widehat\theta-va)^2]
 \ge\frac{a^2}{4}\exp\{-\operatorname{KL}(P_+\|P_-)\}. \tag{17}
\]

For the parametric floor, take singleton observed and latent state spaces, a binary action alphabet, and \(b=e=(1/2,1/2)\).  Make the state transition constant and, independently over time, draw \(Y_t\in\{-M_1,+M_1\}\) with
\[
 \Pr_v(Y_t=y)=\frac12\left(1+\frac{y}{M_1}\frac{v}{4\sqrt T}\right),
 \qquad v\in\{-1,+1\}. \tag{18}
\]
The state contraction coefficient is zero, \(d_e=d_b\), and the action ratio is one.  Furthermore
\[
 |E_vY_t|=\frac{M_1}{4\sqrt T}\le M_1,
 \qquad E_vY_t^2=M_1^2<M_2, \tag{19}
\]
so both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\) for every \(C\ge1\).  Their target values are \(\pm a_T\), where \(a_T=M_1/(4\sqrt T)\).  With \(u_T=1/(4\sqrt T)\), direct calculation and \(\log(1+z)\le z\) give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_+^T\|P_-^T)
 =Tu_T\log\frac{1+u_T}{1-u_T}
 \le\frac{2Tu_T^2}{1-u_T}\le\frac14. \tag{20}
\]
The last inequality uses \(0<u_T\le1/4\).  Applying (17) yields a constant \(c_1>0\), depending only on \(M_1\), such that
\[
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\ge c_1T^{-1},
 \qquad C\ge1. \tag{21}
\]

It remains to obtain the hidden-state term uniformly in \(C\).  For \(C>1\), the amplitude in \(\mathrm{def{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}family}\) satisfies
\[
 \frac12q_C\le\varepsilon_C\le q_C. \tag{22}
\]
Indeed, if \(1<C\le2\), then \(\varepsilon_C=(C-1)/2\) and \(\varepsilon_C/q_C=C/2\in(1/2,1]\).  If \(C\ge2\), then \(\varepsilon_C=1/2\), while \(q_C\in[1/2,1)\), which again proves (22).  This argument uses no limit in \(C\).

Take the signed-depth construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}family}\), whose scaled Rademacher reward has support \(\{-M_1,+M_1\}\).  Its dimensionless emission signal is
\[
 \gamma_0:=\frac{c_0}{M_1}=\frac{1-\alpha}{4}\in(0,1/4).
\]
The stationary formulas in \(\mathrm{lem{:}signed\text{-}depth\text{-}membership}\) apply, and the reward moments satisfy
\[
 |E_v[Y_t\mid J_t,U_t,A_t]|\le c_0=M_1\gamma_0<M_1,
 \qquad E_v[Y_t^2\mid J_t,U_t,A_t]=M_1^2<M_2. \tag{23}
\]
Thus these alternatives belong to the conditional-moment class.  They use one observed state, the binary-action subclass of the allowed finite action alphabets, and \(2(Q+1)\) latent states.  Their target values are
\[
 \theta_v=v a_Q,
 \qquad a_Q:=c_0\varepsilon_Cw_Q. \tag{24}
\]

We expose the radius in the observed-law divergence instead of absorbing it into a constant.  Standardizing rewards by the positive number \(M_1\) is a measurable bijection of the observed experiment.  Hence the filter identities of \(\mathrm{lem{:}observed\text{-}path\text{-}kl}\), applied to \(Y_t/M_1\), give
\[
 \frac{E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]}{M_1}
 =v\gamma_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v,
 \qquad q_t^v\le K_0\alpha^Q. \tag{25}
\]
Every conditional reward probability is strictly positive because \(\gamma_0<1/4\), so all conditional divergences are well defined.  For Rademacher laws with means \(m,n\in(-1,1)\), \(\log z\le z-1\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Rad}(m)\|\operatorname{Rad}(n)\}
 \le\frac{(m-n)^2}{1-n^2}. \tag{26}
\]
The action laws are identical under the two alternatives.  The chain rule for their finite product densities, (25)--(26), and the bound \(|\gamma_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v|\le\gamma_0\) therefore give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le \frac{4\gamma_0^2\varepsilon_C^2K_0^2}{1-\gamma_0^2}
       \alpha^{2Q}\sum_{t=1}^TE[(a_t^{(Q)})^2]. \tag{27}
\]
Under the signed-depth behavior policy the actions are independent Bernoulli variables with success probability \(L^{-1}\).  With \(\ell_t=\min\{Q,t-1\}\), including every stationary initial window,
\[
 E[(a_t^{(Q)})^2]
 =L^{-(2Q-\ell_t)}\le L^{-Q}. \tag{28}
\]
Define
\[
 \overline B:=\frac{4\gamma_0^2K_0^2}{1-\gamma_0^2}<\infty. \tag{29}
\]
The inequalities \(\gamma_0<1\) and \(K_0<\infty\) justify (29), and \(\overline B\) depends only on \(t_0\).  Equations (27)--(29) prove the uniform modulus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le\overline B\,T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}. \tag{30}
\]

Choose a finite \(x_0\ge1\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta\), large enough that
\[
 Q_x:=\left\lceil D^{-1}\log(8\overline Bx)\right\rceil\ge1
 \quad\text{whenever }x\ge x_0. \tag{31}
\]
By (22), (30), and \(\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}=e^{-DQ}\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q_x,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\|\mathbb P_{Q_x,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})
 \le\overline Bx e^{-DQ_x}\le\frac18. \tag{32}
\]
The stationary depth mass satisfies
\[
 w_{Q_x}=\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^{Q_x}}{1-\alpha^{Q_x+1}}
 \ge(1-\alpha)\alpha^{Q_x}. \tag{33}
\]
The ceiling in (31) and (10) also imply
\[
 \alpha^{2Q_x}\ge\alpha^2(8\overline Bx)^{-\beta}. \tag{34}
\]
Apply (17) with (24), then use (22) and (32)--(34).  A constant \(c_2>0\), depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1\), satisfies, for \(x\ge x_0\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)
 &\ge c_2q_C^2x^{-\beta}\\
 &=c_2T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}.
 \end{split}\tag{35}
\]
The lower pair is contained in the binary bounded-reward subclass, so (35) transfers to the larger finite-action conditional-moment class by monotonicity of the supremum.

When \(x<x_0\), the hidden-state expression obeys
\[
 T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}=T^{-1}x^{1-\beta}
 \le x_0^{1-\beta}T^{-1}, \tag{36}
\]
and is therefore controlled by the parametric lower bound (21).  When \(x\ge x_0\), the maximum of (21) and (35) is at least half their sum.  This proves the lower inequality with a constant independent of \(C\).  Together with (14), it proves the displayed uniform risk law.

Finally, the ratio of the hidden-state term to the parametric term is
\[
 \frac{T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}}{T^{-1}}
 =(Tq_C^2)^{1-\beta}. \tag{37}
\]
Because \(0<\beta<1\), (37) is bounded at \(q_C=O(T^{-1/2})\) and diverges when \(Tq_C^2\to\infty\).  Also \(q_C=(C-1)/C\sim C-1\) as \(C\downarrow1\).  These identities prove the claimed elbow, the stated history length, and the absence of a logarithmic risk factor.
body.justification: The theorem gives one cardinality- and radius-uniform minimax law joining exact stationary equality, shrinking latent overlap, and every fixed overlap radius.
body.gap: HuWager2023 supplies the unrestricted POMDP exponent but leaves an overlapping hidden-state hard family open and does not give a stationary-overlap-radius phase diagram.
body.consumer: In the finite-state insulin-policy adaptation, a latent physiological-occupancy assurance shortens the optimal history only through the quantitative radius \(q_C\); it yields immediate weighting at the parametric order only at the \(T^{-1/2}\) elbow.
